key_insight: For geometry-aware hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and physical consistency constraints are more effective during fine-tuning than during early or full-training use.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable patient-specific aortic flow prediction while highlighting the importance of training geometries that cover intended clinical anatomies.
method: Generate synthetic aortic CFD solutions with automatically adjusted, physiologically consistent boundary conditions.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields from a common reference and predict peak-systolic velocity and pressure using Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net models.
Evaluate active learning and differentiable finite element residual constraints to improve data efficiency and physical consistency.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports fine-tuning gains from gradient- and subspace-based acquisition and physical consistency objectives, while out-of-distribution tests identify geometric coverage as the primary limitation.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the geometry parametrization's support remains limited; the abstract provides no numerical error or speedup estimates.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
